title: Running-process kill test never verifies termination
reasoning: The test calls kill() without asserting that the process is alive beforehand or terminated afterward. Replacing kill() with a no-op can still pass because cleanup runs afterward. Additionally, next() on a silent sleep command with timeout=None does not establish a reliable readiness signal and may wait until the command has already finished.
reproduction: Make kill() a no-op: this test contains no termination assertion that would detect the regression.
recommendation: Use an explicit readiness event from a long-running child, retain its process handle, assert it is running, invoke kill(), and assert termination within a bounded deadline before cleanup.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The sibling kill test only checks safety when no process exists. Timeout tests exercise a different entry point and do not establish that explicit kill() terminates an active process.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand this lifecycle scenario to prove readiness and bounded termination, with guaranteed cleanup and explicit stream closure even when assertions fail.
